# `scikitplot.decile`

<!-- Generated by `python tools/maint_tools/generate_usage_skills.py sync` from the installed package; edit the module's docstrings or `__all__`, not this file. -->

Visualizing predictive model insights for enhanced business decision-making.

## Install

```sh
pip install scikit-plots
```

## Public API

Declared in `scikitplot.decile.__all__`, in that order.

| Name | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `ModelPlotPy` | class | Decile/ntile analysis for sklearn classifiers. |
| `plot_response` | function | Plot response curve. |
| `plot_cumresponse` | function | Plot cumulative response curve. |
| `plot_cumlift` | function | Plot cumulative lift curve. |
| `plot_cumgains` | function | Plot cumulative gains curve. |
| `plot_all` | function | Plot response, cumulative response, cumulative lift, and cumulative gains as a 2x2 panel. |
| `plot_costsrevs` | function | Plot costs and revenues curves. |
| `plot_profit` | function | Plot profit curve. |
| `plot_roi` | function | Plot ROI (return on investment) curve. |
| `summarize_selection` | function | Return a standardized summary row per group at a selected ntile. |

All names with signatures: [references/API.md](references/API.md).

## Example (from the docstring of `scikitplot.decile.ModelPlotPy`)

```pycon
>>> from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
>>> X = pd.DataFrame({"x": [0, 1, 2, 3]})
>>> y = pd.Series([0, 0, 1, 1])
>>> m = LogisticRegression().fit(X, y)
>>> mp = ModelPlotPy([X], [y], ["train"], [m], ["lr"], ntiles=2)
>>> scores = mp.prepare_scores_and_ntiles()
>>> set(scores.columns) >= {
...     "dataset_label",
...     "model_label",
...     "target_class",
...     "prob_0",
...     "prob_1",
...     "dec_0",
...     "dec_1",
... }
True
```
